answer: Persistent State Taper: an identity's influence decays on a glacier curve tied to its continuous spend, not a one-time fee. Duplicate identities face basalt-hard marginal costs because each clone must independently sustain that decay or be trivially excluded. Attacker cost scales linearly per identity per period, while honest single identities amortize across volume—the dune of clones collapses under sustained per-identity overhead.
